newsitem.title: USA: Amerijet to fly Los Angeles to Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Amerijet to fly Los Angeles to Mexico.

text.p: Amerijet International Inc, the Fort Lauderdale all-cargo carrier, expects to begin service from Los Angeles International Airport to Mexico within a few months, an official told Reuters Friday.

"We have to get Mexico authority," Pam Rollins, vice president of Amerijet, said Friday. Amerijet recently received U.S. Department of Transportation approval. "We don't anticipate begining service until the second second quarter," Rollins said.

Privately-held Amerijet has had road feeder service out of Los Angeles but has not flown to international destinations from there. Amerijet flew a domestic freighter service along the West Coast until 1990, but abandoned it after jet fuel prices shot up follwing the Gulf War, Rollins said.
Its route is likely to be Miami-Mexico City-Guadalajara-Los Angeles-Mexico City and then perhaps Merida and back to Miami, Rollins said.

Amerijet, which operates Boeing 727s, ranks eighth in freight through its hub of Miami International Airport, according to statistics compiled by the Dade County Aviation Department. Amierjet carried 55,115 tons of freight at Miami in 1995, up 35 percent from 1994.
Amerijet has been expanding recently, adding the Dominican Republic in September.
